svg.text: Removal: one commit makes a share gone to clients; recorded, resumable steps do the rest.
DeleteShare(share, snapshots)
disposition: refuse, delete, detach
refused, nothing changed
a cut is running: ErrDelay · a GC pause on a namespace the share names: ErrMoving
snapshots exist and the request neither deletes nor detaches them
delete while a use record exists, or a snapshot is locked (ErrLocked)
the share is already being removed or retired: ErrStale
1 Mark: one transaction
tracked reads of nsg, its namespaces' GC pauses and rh; GuardRange S‖id‖snap‖ and S‖id‖use‖
state → being removed; delete NX‖share‖name and NP‖path; end a running re-home; raise SL
DeleteShare returns here
every call into the share: ErrStale
a new share may take the name at once
2 Snapshots
delete: each through RFC 12's serial deletion · detach: nothing deleted yet
progress: S‖id‖st
steps 3 and 4 run on every shard of the share, each driven by that shard's primary
3 Live state and journal
join every call in flight; DropShare ends every open, lock and grant without a recall
with detach, first offload what a kept snapshot's hold marks cover; then rm = offloaded
once every shard is offloaded: replicated Forget of the share's tag; then rm = forgotten
SH‖shard‖rm: offloaded,
forgotten
st enters its forget phase only once
every shard's rm is offloaded
4 Files
drop every file under F‖ShareID in bounded batches, each ref by RFC 6's batched removal
SH‖shard‖rm: step 4, done
st passes step 4 only in the batch
that finds the last shard done
5 Server-wide rows that name the share
grants and GR keys · share-scoped CFG, raising CFGGEN · CL‖client‖sh‖shard · MV; parked refs stay
progress: S‖id‖st
6 The share's own records, then its shards
every S‖id‖* but st, then each SH‖shard with its rq, rqx, xh, hw, fw and rm rows
last transaction: the root's shard record with st and nsg; raises SL, runs step 7's check
with detach: st → retired, and what RFC 12 §2.8 still reads stays
S‖id‖st deleted last,
or retired with detach
7 The namespace
once nothing RFC 9 §7.6's drain gate reads names it: drain mark, then that section's steps 1–3
NS‖ns‖drain
Each step is idempotent. The coordinator, the primary of the shard holding the share's root, records steps 1, 2 and 5–7 in S‖id‖st; a crash
or failover resumes each part where its record says it stopped. The coordinator advances st over the shard list S‖id‖shs in batches within K.
